source_title: SCCM Guidelines on Recognizing and Responding to Clinical Deterioration Outside the ICU
clinical_context: Use when multiple measurements suggest new deterioration or failure to improve after an intervention.
key_points: Clinical deterioration is described as potentially reversible morbidity and mortality when recognized and responded to early.
Focused education for bedside clinicians in signs of deterioration is suggested by the panel.
Use this card to explain why trend-based alerts should be reviewed by humans.
risk_use_note: General deterioration source only; does not define shock, ARDS, respiratory failure, or AKI.
time_window_hint: Prefer repeated evidence in last 1-6 hours depending on agent configuration.
allowed_summary_language: The recent trajectory appears worse and should be interpreted by the clinical team.

evidence_location.quote: Clinical deterioration of patients hospitalized outside the ICU is a source of potentially reversible morbidity and mortality.
